subject: the architecture judgements wave monitors have actually issued, each pinned to the wave receipt that grounded it and to the real judged diff it was issued against
detector: the default, and what a precedent declaring no `kind` gets: regex over the ADDED lines of a diff; a match is a question, never a verdict. Acquittal patterns are searched over the added lines of the SAME FILE, never over unchanged context and never pooled across the diff - context that merely mentions the right word does not exculpate a shape the diff introduced, and one file's exculpation is not another's.

detector_kinds.unread-field: a field ADDED to a data file whose every ADDED mention in code is a refusal line. Declared, validated, and read by nothing.

reading: A signal is a reason to ask the clause's question with the matched bytes quoted. This bundle reads and questions; it runs no falsification experiment and issues no verdict.

precedents.title: an abstraction, field or config key no process resolves
precedents.question: which process resolves this field? name it, or delete the field rather than demoting it to a comment

provenance.quote: Wave-17 monitor review of b72-bootstrap raised three defects in the entry shape. authorized_head and refs were validated with their own diagnostics and never read by anything: a grep of the branch finds each field only inside its own validation. A documented pin no process resolves is the exact failure this repository admits skills to detect, so both are deleted rather than demoted to comments.

precedents.title: boring over clever: a mechanism that needs an explanation to read as correct
precedents.question: a path prefix test is a binding only when the path cannot lie about where it points - what normalises this one?

provenance.quote: Wave-17 monitor review of b72-bootstrap: skills/<skill>/../../scripts/anything.py satisfied the prefix test that was supposed to bind an entry to its own Skill's tree. A prefix is only a binding when a path cannot lie about where it points, so no argv part may be absolute or carry a spelling normpath would change.

reproduces: elif not any(part.startswith(f"skills/{skill}/") for part in argv):

precedents.title: availability is not use: a convention only author memory re-reads
precedents.question: the machine-read column moved for every row; did the prose that describes it move too, and what re-reads that prose?

provenance.quote: Three row notes in domain/capability-topology.json landed still reasoning in the numbering the same atom had just retired. Every arrival value moved mechanically with the rename; the free text did not, because nothing read it. That is clause A4's own shape - a documented claim whose subject no longer carries it - inside the ledger that names A4, so the cure is a reader rather than a careful pass.

precedents.title: the smallest diff that satisfies the issue, and no gate widened to fit it

provenance.quote: Changing the check's expected authoring_command and the receipts' actual value in the same PR is checked by the old, not-yet-merged validator, which still expects the old string -- CI caught this immediately (AUTHORING_COMMAND_INVALID on all five Skills). Filed ed3c/skill-concerns#44 with the two-PR sequence this actually needs.

precedents.title: a restated copy of another owner's ceremony, where a pointer belongs

precedents.title: ambient versus admitted: a dependency with no pin and no digest
precedents.question: this reaches a host tool or a host path with no pin and no digest - which admitted bytes does it read, and what re-resolves them?

provenance.quote: harness layer: the actors were driven by `claude -p` on the operator's own machine, so the arm-without floor depends on that host's settings. --setting-sources "" was readback-probed once and reported no user-level memory loaded; that probe is a one-time observation with no standing reader, and a campaign re-run on a differently configured host would move the control arm without anything going red
